newsitem.title: UK: EBRD meeting resumes after false alarm.
newsitem.headline: EBRD meeting resumes after false alarm.

text.p: Police evacuated the annual meeting of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) in London's historic Guildhall on Monday after fire alarms went off, but later said it had been a false alarm.
"It was a fire alarm, a false alarm and they have gone back in now," a spokeswoman for the City of London police told Reuters.
A police officer at the Guildhall said the alarm was believed to have been set off accidentally by contractors.
EBRD Chairman Ruairi Quinn, the Irish finance minister, had earlier asked delegates to leave at around 1200 GMT, asking them to return at 1400 GMT.
The EBRD, set up in 1991 to help former Soviet bloc countries make the transition to market economies, had earlier begun its two-day annual meeting.
Preliminary weekend events, including seminars and business presentations, were marred by long queues for admission and overcrowding in meeting rooms at a separate venue in the City of London.
